Most startups don’t die from competition. They die from scaling the wrong thing too early.

I’ve watched founders pour $50k into ads before they had a product people actually re-buy.
Growth hides broken operations. It doesn’t fix them.

Before you scale, pressure-test three things:

→ Can you deliver 10x the volume without you in the room?
→ Do your unit economics survive a discount war?
→ Would your best customer refer you, unprompted?

If the answer is “not yet” — you don’t have a growth problem. You have a foundation problem.
